sentence: Vertigo is the feeling that you or the room is spinning, and the NHS says inner ear problems are its most common causes.
The NHS says to call 999 for vertigo with double vision, trouble speaking or weakness or numbness in an arm or leg.
note: Summary of NHS vertigo page 999 advice

sentence: A severe headache or feeling very sick with vertigo calls for an urgent GP appointment or NHS 111.
Dizziness that keeps coming back, or comes with hearing, eyesight or pulse changes or fainting, is a reason to contact a GP.
Dizziness is a broad word that people use for several sensations, including light-headedness and a feeling of spinning.
note: NHS inform page covers dizziness (lightheadedness); the umbrella-word framing is a gloss

sentence: Vertigo is a particular kind of dizziness in which it feels as if you or the room is spinning, even when nothing is moving.
The NHS says inner ear problems, which affect balance, are the most common causes of vertigo.
NHS inform lists labyrinthitis, migraine, stress or anxiety, low blood sugar, dehydration and certain prescription medicines among the causes of dizziness.
A sudden drop in blood pressure on standing up is another listed cause.
Less often, an irregular heart rhythm called atrial fibrillation, or carbon monoxide poisoning, is on the list.
note: NHS inform page lists atrial fibrillation and carbon monoxide poisoning

sentence: The NHS vertigo page lists benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV), labyrinthitis, vestibular neuritis, Ménière’s disease and migraine, and notes that some medicines can also cause it.
note: Search summary of the NHS vertigo page

sentence: In BPPV, certain head movements trigger spells of spinning that usually last from a few seconds to a few minutes.
note: MedlinePlus BPPV page; wording of duration comes from search summary of BPPV sources

sentence: Rolling over in bed or tilting the head back to look up are typical triggers.
Labyrinthitis is usually caused by a viral infection such as a cold or flu, so antibiotics will not help, and the vertigo usually lasts a few days.
Hearing loss and ringing in the ears (tinnitus) can come with labyrinthitis.
Ménière’s disease is a rarer cause, with attacks that can include tinnitus, a feeling of fullness in the ear and changing hearing; the NHS says there is no cure but symptoms can be managed.
note: Search summary of the NHS Ménière’s page

sentence: NHS inform advises contacting a GP if dizziness will not go away or keeps coming back.
Changes in hearing, eyesight or pulse, or fainting, are further reasons to make contact.
For vertigo, the NHS suggests seeing a GP if it comes on suddenly, does not go away, keeps returning or affects daily life.
note: Search summary of NHS vertigo page

sentence: The NHS says to ask for an urgent GP appointment or call NHS 111 if vertigo comes with a severe headache, being sick or feeling very sick, or a very high temperature.
It says to call 999 or go to A&E if vertigo comes with double vision or loss of vision, hearing loss, trouble speaking, or weakness, numbness or tingling in an arm or a leg.
The NHS also advises not to drive yourself to A&E.
note: NHS stroke guidance: do not drive yourself to A&E

sentence: Dizziness is among the symptoms the NHS lists for stroke, and any sign of stroke is treated as an emergency: the NHS FAST test stands for face, arms, speech and time to call 999.
